To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the duodenum-preserving resections are superior to the classic Whipple procedure with regard to postoperative morbidity and mortality; 2) the duodeno-pancreatic resections are superior with regard to post-operative pain relief; and 3) the long-term outcome in terms of pain relief is superior for the duodenum preserving resections.
duodenum-preserving resections are associated with a shorter hospital stay and a better quality of life compared to a standard resection with pancreatic transection.
